definitions.explanation: Secretly planning with others to commit an illegal or harmful act. A legal term that became widely known through political debate over the '{共謀罪|きょうぼうざい}' (conspiracy law) in Japan.

examples.japanese: {共謀|きょうぼう}して{犯行|はんこう}に{及|およ}んだ。
examples.english: They conspired and committed the crime.

examples.japanese: {共謀罪|きょうぼうざい}をめぐる{議論|ぎろん}が{国会|こっかい}で{行|おこな}われた。
examples.english: Debate over the conspiracy law took place in the Diet.

examples.japanese: {二人|ふたり}は{共謀|きょうぼう}の{疑|うたが}いで{逮捕|たいほ}された。
examples.english: The two were arrested on suspicion of conspiracy.

notes: Used with する: {共謀|きょうぼう}する (to conspire). The term gained wide public attention through debates over Japan's {共謀罪|きょうぼうざい} (conspiracy crime) legislation, formally part of the {組織的犯罪処罰法|そしきてきはんざいしょばつほう} (Act on Punishment of Organized Crimes). Common collocations: {共謀|きょうぼう}{共同正犯|きょうどうせいはん} (co-conspiracy), {共謀|きょうぼう}の{疑|うたが}い (suspicion of conspiracy). Related: {陰謀|いんぼう} (plot, secret scheme) is broader and can refer to political intrigue, not just criminal conspiracy.
